Dandridge was found at the brownstone. The cigarette he had going burned itself out on the sill where it fell. The bells rang the half hour at 11:00 PM. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.
The coroner puts death between 10:00 PM and 11:30 PM — two hours of nothing useful. One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.
A nickel-plated revolver is gone from the speakeasy. The drawer it was kept in is open and the oiled cloth is still in it.
Hochstetter puts Dandridge at the speakeasy while the fight was on the radio, which was 10:30 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.
Hochstetter was at the speakeasy at 11:00 PM and heard a shot from the direction of the brownstone, while the bells were going.
Pickering was at the speakeasy at 11:00 PM and heard a shot from the direction of the brownstone, while the bells were going.
Found at the brownstone: A draft codicil in Dandridge’s hand striking Hargrove out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Rosenbaum says Dandridge told Hargrove the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Found at the brownstone: A subpoena naming Dandridge before the grand jury, with Hanrahan’s name written in the margin.
Rosenbaum says Dandridge said to Hanrahan that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found at the brownstone: A lease assignment made out in Petrosino’s name, waiting only on Dandridge’s signature.
Hanrahan says Dandridge told Petrosino the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Found at the parlour: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Lindemann, endorsed to Dandridge, three months past due.
Hanrahan says Dandridge told Lindemann that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Brennan hired us, and wants it known that Hanrahan needed Dandridge silent before the grand jury, and would rather we started there.
